```go
package ledger

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// Refactor log:
//
// The original implementation was a single 200-line function that sorted with a
// hand-rolled bubble sort, formatted every row in a goroutine that communicated
// over an unbuffered channel, and validated currency/locale/date through a
// recursive self-call plus scattered inline checks. It was rewritten as a small
// set of focused helpers:
//
//  1. Validate currency and locale up front with isCurrency/isLocale.
//  2. Copy the input and sort it with sort.Slice (date, then description, then
//     change) instead of the manual bubble sort. The copy guarantees the caller's
//     slice is never mutated.
//  3. Build the header with header(locale).
//  4. Format each row with formatLine, which delegates to formatDate, truncate
//     and formatChange.
//
// The goroutine/channel machinery was removed; rows are built sequentially into
// a strings.Builder. Behavior (including the exact column widths and the rune-
// based padding of the change column) is unchanged, so the existing test suite
// still passes.

type Entry struct {
	Date        string // "Y-m-d"
	Description string
	Change      int // in cents
}

const (
	dateWidth        = 10
	descriptionWidth = 25
	changeWidth      = 13
)

var (
	errInvalidCurrency = errors.New("invalid currency")
	errInvalidLocale   = errors.New("invalid locale")
	errInvalidDate     = errors.New("invalid date")
)

// FormatLedger renders a formatted ledger for the given currency and locale.
func FormatLedger(currency string, locale string, entries []Entry) (string, error) {
	if !isCurrency(currency) {
		return "", errInvalidCurrency
	}
	if !isLocale(locale) {
		return "", errInvalidLocale
	}

	sorted := make([]Entry, len(entries))
	copy(sorted, entries)
	sort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {
		if sorted[i].Date != sorted[j].Date {
			return sorted[i].Date < sorted[j].Date
		}
		if sorted[i].Description != sorted[j].Description {
			return sorted[i].Description < sorted[j].Description
		}
		return sorted[i].Change < sorted[j].Change
	})

	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(header(locale))
	for _, e := range sorted {
		line, err := formatLine(currency, locale, e)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		b.WriteString(line)
	}
	return b.String(), nil
}

func isCurrency(currency string) bool {
	return currency == "USD" || currency == "EUR"
}

func isLocale(locale string) bool {
	return locale == "en-US" || locale == "nl-NL"
}

func header(locale string) string {
	dateCol, descCol, changeCol := "Date", "Description", "Change"
	if locale == "nl-NL" {
		dateCol, descCol, changeCol = "Datum", "Omschrijving", "Verandering"
	}
	return pad(dateCol, dateWidth) + " | " + pad(descCol, descriptionWidth) + " | " + changeCol + "\n"
}

func formatLine(currency, locale string, e Entry) (string, error) {
	date, err := formatDate(locale, e.Date)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return pad(date, dateWidth) + " | " + truncate(e.Description) + " | " +
		rightPad(formatChange(currency, locale, e.Change), changeWidth) + "\n"
}

// formatDate converts a "YYYY-MM-DD" date to the locale's display format,
// returning errInvalidDate when the input is malformed.
func formatDate(locale, date string) (string, error) {
	if len(date) != 10 || date[4] != '-' || date[7] != '-' {
		return "", errInvalidDate
	}
	year, month, day := date[0:4], date[5:7], date[8:10]
	if locale == "nl-NL" {
		return day + "-" + month + "-" + year, nil
	}
	return month + "/" + day + "/" + year, nil
}

// truncate shortens descriptions longer than the column width, appending an
// ellipsis, and pads shorter ones with trailing spaces.
func truncate(s string) string {
	if len(s) > descriptionWidth {
		return s[:22] + "..."
	}
	return pad(s, descriptionWidth)
}

// formatChange renders a change in cents using the locale's number format.
func formatChange(currency, locale string, change int) string {
	negative := change < 0
	if negative {
		change = -change
	}
	units := change / 100
	cents := change % 100

	symbol := "$"
	if currency == "EUR" {
		symbol = "€"
	}

	if locale == "nl-NL" {
		// "$ 1.234,56" for credits, "$ 123,45-" for debits.
		return symbol + " " + groupDigits(strconv.Itoa(units), ".") + "," +
			fmt.Sprintf("%02d", cents) + signSuffix(negative)
	}
	// "$1,234.56" for credits, "($1,234.56)" for debits.
	if negative {
		return "(" + symbol + groupDigits(strconv.Itoa(units), ",") + "." +
			fmt.Sprintf("%02d", cents) + ")"
	}
	return symbol + groupDigits(strconv.Itoa(units), ",") + "." +
		fmt.Sprintf("%02d", cents) + " "
}

// groupDigits inserts sep as a thousands separator, e.g. "1234567" -> "1.234.567".
func groupDigits(s, sep string) string {
	var parts []string
	for len(s) > 3 {
		parts = append(parts, s[len(s)-3:])
		s = s[:len(s)-3]
	}
	parts = append(parts, s)
	for i, j := 0, len(parts)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
		parts[i], parts[j] = parts[j], parts[i]
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, sep)
}

func signSuffix(negative bool) string {
	if negative {
		return "-"
	}
	return " "
}

// pad left-justifies s to width by adding trailing spaces.
func pad(s string, width int) string {
	return s + strings.Repeat(" ", width-len(s))
}

// rightPad right-justifies s to width by adding leading spaces, counting runes
// so multi-byte symbols such as "€" occupy a single column.
func rightPad(s string, width int) string {
	return strings.Repeat(" ", width-utf8.RuneCountInString(s)) + s
}
```

## What I did

I read `.docs/instructions.md` (a refactoring exercise) and rewrote `ledger.go` cleanly while preserving the exact behavior the tests check. `ledger_test.go` was untouched and no new files were created.

The original was a single ~200-line function that:
- sorted with a hand-rolled bubble sort built from boolean lookup maps,
- validated currency/locale via a recursive self-call for the empty-ledger case plus scattered inline checks,
- formatted each row in its own goroutine over an unbuffered channel.

I replaced it with small focused helpers:
- `isCurrency` / `isLocale` — validate inputs up front (replacing the recursive hack).
- A `copy` + `sort.Slice` by date → description → change (the copy guarantees the caller's slice is never mutated, satisfying `TestFormatLedgerNotChangeInput`).
- `header` — locale-specific column headings.
- `formatLine` → `formatDate`, `truncate`, `formatChange` — one row at a time into a `strings.Builder`.

Behavior preserved exactly, including the subtle bits: column widths (10/25/13), rune-based right-padding of the change column so `€` counts as one column, and the per-locale number formats (US `$1,234.56` / `($1,234.56)` vs Dutch `$ 1.234,56 ` / `$ 123,45-`).

Per the spec, I added a refactor log as a comment at the top of `ledger.go` describing the changes.
